svg.text: Collection path: Apps / K8s nodes → OTel SDK / Agent → OTel Collector → backends (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Tempo/Jaeger, Loki/Elasticsearch).

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Backends are query/store systems. The collector is the always-on control-plane hop that fans out telemetry. Agents run on every node (data plane adjacency, control purpose).

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: SLIs (RPS, latency, error rate, saturation) are derived here and drive HPA, canary analysis, and paging — not a dashboard graveyard.

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Feedback to engineering · observability is not a dead end

svg.text: • A bad deploy is visible as a burn-rate alert and a canary metric shift — Argo CD / gitops rollback is the remediation, not a CI re-run of “deploy.sh”.

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • HPA and Cluster Autoscaler consume metrics from this plane (CPU, RPS, custom). Scale-out is not a Terraform apply and not a CI job.

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Platform team uses the same telemetry for control-plane health (Argo CD sync, API server latency, image-pull errors, admission denials).

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Product engineers get paged on their SLOs; they do not SSH to nodes. The numbered delivery path and this feedback path are how the organization learns.

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • Capacity planning (new node groups, bigger DBs) feeds back into plane B: Terraform. That is the rare, deliberate infra change — not the daily feature path.

text.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: • OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral collection layer; backends above are interchangeable stores/UX. Do not emit three competing agent stacks per pod.
